project.title: Performance evaluation, key enzymatic activity, antioxidant response and metagenomic analysis of sequencing batch reactor under long-term exposure of low ciprofloxacin concentration
project.description: Ciprofloxacin is a widely used antibiotic that is frequently detected at low concentrations in wastewater. Long-term exposure to such low levels may affect the performance of biological wastewater treatment systems. In this study, a sequencing batch reactor (SBR) was operated for 188 days and exposed to 100 ug/L ciprofloxacin from day 21 onward. We evaluated nitrogen removal performance, key enzymatic activities, antioxidant responses, microbial community succession, and antibiotic resistance genes (ARGs) using metagenomic analysis. The results showed that although ammonium removal efficiency remained stable, nitrogen conversion rates and the activities of key enzymes (AMO, NOR, NR, and NIR) gradually declined. Reactive oxygen species (ROS) and antioxidant enzyme activities increased, indicating oxidative stress. Microbial community structure changed significantly, with decreases in nitrifying bacteria and some denitrifying genera. Nitrogen metabolism genes were downregulated, while ARGs and mobile genetic elements were enriched. These findings help to understand the linkage among nitrogen removal, microbial ecology, and resistance genes in bioreactors under long-term exposure to low antibiotic concentrations, and provide a basis for process optimization and risk prevention.
